newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's 'Mr Yen' promoted to new post.
newsitem.headline: Japan's 'Mr Yen' promoted to new post.

text.p: Influential Japanese finance official Eisuke Sakakibara is to be promoted to vice minister for international affairs, a senior finance ministry official said on Friday.
Sakakibara's widely anticipated appointment will become official on July 15, following cabinet approval, the official told reporters.
Sakakibara, currently director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, has been dubbed "Mr Yen" by the media for his influence over currency markets.

His promotion will put him in formal charge of Finance Ministry negotiations with other Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations, and is seen as a recognition of his success in turning around the yen's precipitous rise to around 80 yen to the dollar in 1995.

Sakakibara was also instrumental in revising Japan's foreign exchange laws as a step toward Tokyo's "Big Bang" financial and regulatory reforms, one of the top initiatives of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's administration.
The current vice finance minister for international affairs, Takatoshi Kato, will retire, the official said.
Haruhiko Kuroda, currently president of the ministry's Institute of Fiscal and Monetary Policy, will succeed Sakakibara at the International Finance Bureau.
